newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW -- U.S. Jan CPI rises 0.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW -- U.S. Jan CPI rises 0.1 pct.

text.p: Following are comments from U.S. economists after the Labor Department reported the Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.1 percent compared to a 0.3-percent jump in December.
Minus food and energy, the index also rose 0.1 percent against a revised 0.2 percent increase the previous month. Economists had expected an overall CPI rise of 0.3 percent.
PHILIP BRAVERMAN, CHIEF ECONOMIST, DKB SECURITIES, INC: The CPI "is a spectacular performance ... This is virtually no inflation at all."
Braverman was speaking on Reuters Financial Television.

KEVIN FLANAGAN, VICE PRESIDENT AND AN ECONOMIST, DEAN WITTER REYONOLDS INC: "We've had above-trend growth, but we are not giving off any inflationary pressures ... As a matter of fact, we just broke a string of consecutive gains of about three-tenths of a percent in CPI.
"It's almost as if you had a slight pullback in the pace of inflation at the consumer level. The (Treasury) market is struggling a little bit with the information," Flanagan added.

RAM BHAGAVATULA, CHIEF FINANCIAL ECONOMIST, CITICORP SECURITIES MARKETS INC: "CPI was better than market forecasts. If you look at the components, the really weak prices were in transportation and entertainment ... It continues to suggest inflation is not an issue for this economy."

NICHOLAS PERNA, CHIEF ECONOMIST, FLEET FINANCIAL SERVICES, HARTFORD, CONN: "This is not only good news, it's spectacularly good news ... My only concern with these numbers is that financial markets are what I would call in 'over-react mode' at this point."

Perna continued: "You know these are great numbers but they're not sustainably great ... But markets are likely to overreact, i.e. that you're likely to see bond yields fall too much and possibly the stock market rise too much on the basis of this. Jubiliation is warranted, but all things in moderation."

JOHN RYDING, MANAGING DIRECTOR AND SENIOR ECONOMIST, BEAR STEARNS & CO INC: "Obviously, these are better-than-expected numbers. We continue to get good CPI data that continue to move down the 12-month change in the core rate."

Ryding added: "January is a little better than trend because of the airline tax effect which pushed airline fares down a little more than 3.0 percent. Core CPI continues to be favorable, and that is the number that the Federal Reserve watches. As long as inflation data continues to remain like this, the Fed should be on hold."
